source.title: OpenUnlearning: Accelerating LLM Unlearning via Unified Benchmarking of Methods and Metrics
source.authors: Vineeth Dorna; Anmol Reddy Mekala; Wenlong Zhao; Andrew McCallum; Zachary Chase Lipton; J. Kolter; Pratyush Maini

record.tranche_reason: The study applies relearning and quantization stress tests to unlearned models and reports changes in knowledge-evaluation metrics. It uses its own metric-robustness measures rather than directly measuring recovered knowledge accuracy.
record.gate_note: The paper reports metric-robustness results for relearning, quantization, and probing. The probing results concern training a language-model head on retain90 and do not test activation-direction ablation. Jailbreak ROUGE and paraphrased metrics are included in metric evaluations, but the paper does not report them as attacks restoring knowledge in unlearned models. Method-ranking results and cited attack results are not rows.
record.test_reason: On ~400 unlearned Llama-3.2-1B TOFU checkpoints, the study relearns on forget10 and applies 4-bit quantization. It reports how far forget-set metrics rise against a retain-model reference (relearning) or the pre-quantization score. The outputs are metric-robustness aggregates (R, Q), not direct recovered-accuracy rates, so they bear on B and D only indirectly.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly wrong emphasis. The authors conclude that Extraction Strength and Exact Memorization are the most reliable metrics. Truth Ratio is highly faithful but less robust. MIA metrics are faithful but not robust. Several metrics signal unlearning while knowledge remains recoverable: many unlearned models relearn faster than retain models, and some show quantization rises. SimNPO and RMU rank best, but rankings are sensitive. The authors do not frame the work as disclaiming behavioural recovery; that clause is the reader's addition.
record.recipe_differences: This is a unified benchmark and metric meta-evaluation, not a direct reproduction of the original methods. It uses a Llama-3.2-1B TOFU forget10 setup, a full-forget10 one-epoch relearning intervention, and 4-bit floating-point quantization; it reports robustness scores of evaluation metrics.
record.method_sensitivity: Relearning results vary by metric. Quantization is tested on checkpoints unlearned with a learning rate of 1 × 10−5, selected because quantization is described as most effective at lower learning rates. Results also depend on filtering for substantial unlearning and at least 80% utility.
record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2025 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
record.problems: The reported intervention outcomes are aggregate metric-robustness scores rather than direct target-knowledge accuracy before and after attack. Results combine diverse unlearning methods and checkpoints, so method-specific recovery cannot be determined from the reported aggregates. The authors note that the benchmark setups make simplifying assumptions and may not reflect realistic learning or unlearning dynamics.
record.rows_left_out: Probing results in Appendix Table 5 are not included because the intervention trains a language-model head on retain90 and evaluates probe metrics; it is not activation-direction ablation or direct recovery under version C. Additional probing figures and metric-faithfulness results do not test the listed recovery versions.

untested.parts: No method is shown to reach near-chance targeted accuracy with retained utility, nor shown to resist attacks.
Relearning on unrelated or loosely related data, a small subset of forget facts, and varying relearning-set size. Only one epoch on the full forget10 set is used.
No activation-direction ablation. Probing (a retain-trained LM head on layer 11) gives P=1 for all metrics, and the authors call it uninformative.
Other bit widths (e.g. 8-bit) and other quantization schemes. Checkpoints unlearned at higher learning rates.
Jailbreak and paraphrase are used only as metrics. No prompt-only recovery is reported against a non-attacked baseline.
No resistant counter-method is proposed or tested.

missing.what: Removing the >=80% utility filter lowers quantization robustness further (more models show post-quantization increases). No values are given.
Per-model before/after scatter of relearning and quantization, showing the fraction of models in the unreliable region (no per-method breakdown).

record.verdict_notes: R and Q are robustness scores of evaluation metrics, clipped at 1 and aggregated over filtered checkpoints. They show the direction of recovery but not its size in accuracy terms. Relearning uses the full forget set, so it is non-benign; the retain-model comparison is what makes it evidence of hidden knowledge. The quantization formula's notation (q = mb/ma) appears inverted relative to the text; low Q is read as metric increase. Method rankings (Tables 3, 6) and faithfulness AUCs are correctly not rows.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test whether a method brings targeted-knowledge accuracy to near chance while preserving general ability and whether attacks then fail.
Relearning is on the full forget10 dataset for one epoch, not unrelated or loosely related examples; it does not compare different relearning-set sizes.
No activation-direction ablation is reported, and the study does not establish that a method blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
The study tests 4-bit floating-point quantization; other bit widths and quantization schemes are not tested.
No prompt-only attack is tested on unlearned models as a knowledge-recovery intervention. Jailbreak ROUGE is used in the metric testbed, not as a reported recovery result.
The study does not test a newer method designed to resist the attacks in the claim.

relation.reason: Its stress-test results bear on versions B and D.

tranche.reason: Different method (metric meta-evaluation with relearning and quantization stress tests) on the same question.

source_check.notes: All 16 values match Table 2 (Quant and Relearn columns). Each metric's R and Q come from a filtered subset (utility drop <=20%, unlearned on that metric), not all ~400 models. Q uses only LR-1e-5 checkpoints and drops further without the utility filter (Fig. 11). The 4 MIA metrics (R 0.40-0.59, Q 0.48-0.61) have no rows. Relearning is on the full forget10, not a small set. R and Q are metric-score ratios, not accuracy recovery.

statements.correction: 2506.12618: utility-filtered Llama-3.2-1B TOFU unlearned checkpoints (per metric), relearned on full forget10 (400 QA) for one epoch at lr 2e-5. Measure: relearning robustness R, the metric-recovery rate relative to retain models. R 0.43-0.70 on 7 of 8 knowledge metrics (ES 0.68, Truth Ratio 0.43); Fig. 9: a significant fraction relearn faster than retain. Para. Prob. R 0.98.
statements.problem: Cites this study only in conditions. It gives no result for it, and the Measures list (loss, KnowMem change, PII P3, steps) leaves out the study's measure. Relearning used the full forget10, not a small set.

statements.correction: Para. Prob. R 0.98 vs 0.43-0.70 on the other seven knowledge metrics; MIA metrics R 0.40-0.59. Study verdicts: B supports (7 knowledge metrics, l0), B limits_scope (Para. Prob., l1).
statements.problem: '0.43-0.70 on other metrics' holds only for the other seven knowledge metrics; MIA-MinK++ R is 0.40. The 'challenges' label misfits this study: its verdict here is limits_scope, and it supports B on 7 of 8 metrics.
none; 'most metrics' holds (R 0.43-0.70 on 10 of the 11 other metrics, MIA-MinK++ 0.40); 0.98 on Para. Prob. correct.

statements.correction: Quantized set: checkpoints unlearned at LR 1e-5, drawn from the ~400-model pool. Models with >20% utility drop or not unlearned on that metric are removed. Quantization: 4-bit FP via BitsAndBytes. Q: ES 0.95, EM 0.92, TR 0.92, Para. ROUGE 0.93, ROUGE 0.93; Probability 0.60, Para. Prob. 0.60, Jailbreak ROUGE 0.85. Without the utility filter, Q drops further (Fig. 11).
statements.problem: Implies the ~400-model pool was all unlearned at LR 1e-5. Q comes only from the LR-1e-5 checkpoints, after the utility and per-metric unlearning filters. All Q values are correct.

statements.correction: Q: ES 0.95, EM 0.92 (memorization metrics, least rise); Probability and Para. Prob. 0.60; MIA metrics 0.48-0.61. Across all 12 metrics Q is 0.48-0.95. The study shows that the TOFU metric matters, not a verbatim-vs-knowledge gap.
statements.problem: 0.60-0.95 spans only the 8 knowledge metrics; MIA-MinK and MIA-LOSS have Q 0.48. Here the memorization metrics ES and EM rise least, so the study doesn't show verbatim recovering more than knowledge QA.
